data.title: Mars Bar from 1991 found – and it's 20g bigger than today's
data.author: RickJWagner
data.article_summary:
英国一家清洁公司在Scunthorpe清理囤积者房屋时，发现了一块1991年生产的玛氏巧克力棒。这块35年前的巧克力重62.5克，而现在同款产品仅重40克，缩水了20多克。

清洁公司负责人Victoria Gordon将新旧对比照片发布到社交媒体后迅速走红，引发了关于"缩水式通胀"的热议。她表示这块巧克力"几乎和我的手一样大"，可能不会丢弃，甚至考虑带它进行"英国巡展"。

玛氏公司回应称，过去35年间基于消费者需求、制造成本和可可价格等因素，对产品尺寸进行了多次调整。这一发现引发了公众对食品包装缩水现象的广泛关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一根1991年的Mars巧克力棒被发现后，引发了关于"缩水通胀"（shrinkflation）现象的广泛讨论。

不同观点：

• **批评缩水通胀派**：认为这是普遍现象，产品不断缩水变贵。快餐汉堡肉饼从1/8磅降至1/10磅，几乎所有产品都在变小或涨价，消费者利益受损。

• **支持缩水派**：认为垃圾食品变小反而是好事。美国37%人口肥胖，1940-50年代可乐瓶很小，现在电影院能买半加仑装。减小垃圾食品份量有益公共健康，这是"缩水通胀的罕见积极案例"。

• **质疑报道框架派**：指出食品报道陷入"双输框架"——产品变小被批评坑害消费者，产品太大又被批评导致肥胖，营养价值却被完全忽略。

• **数据质疑派**：实际查看Amazon UK发现Mars巧克力棒有18g、39.4g、51g等多种规格，质疑60g版本是否真的能证明缩水。

• **新闻价值质疑派**：认为一个在囤积者家中发现的35年前糖果棒不值得成为头条新闻。

补充讨论：有人分享Mars品牌的历史（创始人父子反目，儿子在英国创建Mars棒）；有人提到Open Food Facts自2012年起追踪食品价格和包装变化的"食品考古项目"；还有人关注配料表变化，猜测老版本添加剂更少。

49245023.article_content:
Mars Bar from 1991 found - and it's 20g bigger than today's
3 hours ago
Share
Save
Add as preferred on Google
Eleanor Maslin
East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire
Victoria Gordon
Now and then... the 1991 Mars Bar alongside one from today
A 35-year-old Mars Bar has been found during a house clearance – and the discovery has gone viral amid claims it highlights the effect of "shrinkflation".
The chocolate bar with a best-before date of 1991 was found during a clear-out of a house in Scunthorpe.
Victoria Gordon, who runs the cleaning service, posted a photo on social media of the 62.5g bar alongside one of today's Mars Bars, which is 40g.
"It was nearly as big as my hand, which was kind of why I noticed it," she said.
Victoria Gordon
Victoria Gordon found the old Mars Bar on 5 August
Speaking on
BBC Radio Lincolnshire
, Gordon said: "We were clearing out a hoarder's house and everything we were rooting through was decades old.
"This Mars Bar stood out to me because as I picked it up it was nearly the whole length of my hand.
"I was like, 'Wow, look at the size of that!'"
A Mars spokesperson said: "Over the last 35 years, we have made a number of updates to our bar sizes and pack formats to reflect consumer demand, alongside considering wider external factors such as manufacturing costs and the price of cocoa."
Supplied
The chocolate was found during a house clearance
Gordon, who runs Pocket Rockets, is not sure what she will do with the bar, but she said she might be sitting on a "gold mine".
"I do post some hoarding videos but I've never had anything go this viral," she said.
"It's so fascinating what people find so interesting. I almost put it in the skip [but] I might do a UK tour with it."

data.title: Squeak 6.1
data.author: fniephaus
data.article_summary:
Squeak 6.1（代号"Vanessa"）发布说明摘要：

Squeak 即将迎来30周年，推出6.1版本。主要更新包括：全新的树浏览器，支持分层导航和改进的交互；Objectland（Squeak世界）回归；内核基础设施的重大修复，涉及进程模拟、调度和类重塑；工具集和用户界面的全面改进。

自4年前上一版本以来，合并了1700+补丁和9000+方法变更。GUI框架Morphic进行了大规模升级：树形控件全面优化（颜色、快捷键、过滤、拖放）；文本编辑器增强（链接下划线、引号自动转义）；高DPI和多语言支持改进；大量UI调整和稳定性修复。

本版本纪念Vanessa Freudenberg（1972-2025）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Squeak 6.1 发布引发了对 Smalltalk 教育价值、开发体验、生态兼容性及现代化不足的讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为学习 Smalltalk 能真正理解“面向对象”，类似 Lisp 重塑语言观、Erlang深化并发认知；JavaScript 的许多优点也被认为源自 Smalltalk。
• 早期贡献者祝贺新版发布，并以 SameGame 至今仍保留为例，肯定 Squeak 的历史延续及其衍生生态。
• 开发体验方面，运行时检查对象、从 GUI 控件直接定位代码被高度评价；但评论者也指出，强大内省能力可能带来性能代价。
• 有人希望了解 Morphic 的 UI 架构，并询问相关书籍、论文和博客；另有人追问 Squeak 与 Glamorous Toolkit 的差异，体现出对 Smalltalk UI 与工具体系的兴趣。
• 实用性方面，Windows 11 用户遇到杀毒软件误删可执行文件，并询问 Etoys 是否兼容及如何配置。
• 批评者认为 Squeak 长期未解决高 DPI 适配问题，界面像素化且运行缓慢，甚至考虑自行用 Fable 改进。

These release notes are optimized for viewing inside Squeak, as they contain a lot of interactive examples. On this page, interactive links open in SqueakJS, which is a browser-based Smalltalk VM with some limitations. For the best experience, download Squeak and read the release notes there.
Download Squeak
Try it in browser (SqueakJS)
*** Squeak 6.1 "Vanessa" Release Notes ***
As Squeak approaches its 30th anniversary, we are proud to announce the next version of the system, Squeak 6.1. Some highlights of this release are:
A new
tree browser
, which enables navigation through classes and categories using refurbished hierarchical morphs,
The return of
Objectland
(also known as the "Worlds of Squeak"),
Several changes and fixes for the kernel infrastructure for simulating, unwinding, and scheduling processes and reshaping classes,
Miscellaneous improvements and additions to the toolset and user interface for inspecting, debugging, profiling, and versioning code.
Please find below a detailed listing of all the changes, which includes notes on
Major Deprecations
,
Known Issues
, and
Compatibility Notes
at the bottom.
About these release notes.
Phew, what a release! Since the last release
4 years ago
, we have merged
1700+ patches
with
9000+ method changes
. Beyond documenting technical changes in detail, these notes highlight the bigger picture and the overall impact of major developments. Along the way, you will find plenty of links to
code pointers
and
interactive examples
. Thus, these release notes serve not only as a changelog but also as a hands-on guide to exploring new features and mechanisms in Squeak.
Click here
to view an outline of this document.
In memory of Vanessa Freudenberg (1972-2025).

)

tree morphs
:
Improves colors and
mouse and keyboard shortcuts
for navigating trees.
Revises
type-to-filter
similar to lists, highlights search terms, and enables searching single columns via [TAB]. Adds a
configurable filter mode
to search within the current selection, all visible nodes, or the entire tree.
Introduces a recursive "find"/"find again" feature available via [CMD] + [F]/[CMD] + [G].
Adds a
flag
for automatic expansion of trees.
Improves support for
drag'n'drop
by automatically expanding nodes during dragging after one second of hovering.
Miscellaneous stability and performance improvements for layouting, rendering, and event handling in trees.
In the world, supports dropping of
class references
,
system
and
method categories
, and
inspector
and
explorer fields
to display them in a new window/widget.
For mouse interactions, adds new preferences to customize the
double-click time
and
drag thresholds
.

docking bar window menu
, adds an item to collapse windows. Makes

easier to use by expanding the selected window if collapsed. Reorders and decorates items in the
help menu
.

Underlines
links (like this one!)

and

during construction.

theme
support for
progress bars

multilingual support
in different places.

configuration changes,

project view morph
styling, and

.

an issue when profiling code where user events were swallowed.

,
text morphs

scroll panes

data.author: jonathanmkeegan
data.article_summary:
作者从美国NOAA的船只交通数据中收集了超过5万个船名，这些船只通过AIS系统广播身份信息。船名充满了巧妙的双关语、成人笑话以及对影视、文学作品的引用，展现了船主的个性和创造力。

文章按类别展示了各种有趣船名：金融行业相关的如"LIQUID ASSETS"（流动资产）、"BLUE CHIP"（蓝筹股）；法律界的如"CASE CLOSED"（结案）；医学界的如"CADUCEUS"（医学标志）；还有大量带性暗示的双关语船名。

数据显示，美国约12%的家庭拥有船只，养船年均开销1.5-4万美元，船主群体82.9%为白人。这些船名反映了船主的职业、财富水平和文化品味，是政府数据集中人们个性表达的有趣案例。

49243029.article_content:
A smattering of boat names found in NOAA's Marine Cadastre data set. Source:
NOAA
. Visualization: Jon Keegan/Beautiful Public Data.
In the vast ocean of government datasets that I trawl through, I am always on the lookout for moments where people express themselves, leaving behind their own little datum of personality.
These tiny expressions of creativity show up all over public datasets. Air traffic controllers choose
funny names
for airplane navigation waypoints.
Rejected vanity
license plate
registrations turn up in state motor vehicle databases. The names we pick for our dogs appear in local
licensing databases
, and the Social Security Administration even publishes the most
popular names
we give our children. And if you own a boat, you get to name that too.
I went through several years’ worth of NOAA vessel traffic data and pulled a sample of more than 50,000 boat names that were broadcast via Automatic Identification System (AIS) transmitters, which are typically found on larger and commercial vessels. The collection of names is chock full of clever puns, dirty jokes, and references to TV shows, movies, songs, and mythological figures. These names also offer glimpses of the wealth and professions of the people who own a boat.
⛵️🔎 Search all 50,000 boat names, browse by category, or hit random and see what floats to the top 👇🏻
Most commercial vessels 65 feet and over are required to broadcast their precise location and identity using AIS (which lets me make these
cool maps
), but plenty of recreational boaters broadcast anyway, by choice. These names were collected from NOAA’s Marine Cadastre “
broadcast points
” vessel traffic data. NOAA captures AIS data from terrestrial stations along US waterways, so any boat transmitting AIS within range of those stations may show up in the data may show up in this data, though the vast majority don’t transmit a vessel name. Boat owners don’t necessarily have to submit these names to NOAA — AIS vessel names aren’t a comprehensive government registry of boat names. Out of roughly 150,000 unique boats I sampled, only about 50,000 had names.
There are a lot of different kinds of boats in this data, but recreational “pleasure craft” make up about 43% of the boats, followed by cargo ships at 14%. There are also fishing boats, tugs and towboats, passenger ships and ferries, as well as military and search and rescue vessels.
About 12% of US households — roughly 14.5 million — were estimated to own or co-own a recreational boat in 2018, according to a
US Coast Guard survey
.
So who owns boats in the US? The latest edition survey of this survey, from 2018, tells us more about this group. Of boat-owning households, 82.9% were white, while 0.8% were Black or African American.
Boat owners’ lives are reflected in their vessels’ names. Owning a boat is not cheap — yearly expenses can run between
$15,000 and $40,000
.
That leads to plenty of names your favorite hedge fund manager might slap on a yacht:
LIQUID ASSETS
,
BLUE CHIP III
,
PORT FOLIO
,
TRADE DESK
,
RISK & REWARD
,
MUTUAL FUN
,
401(PLAY)
.

,

And plenty of names your doctor or surgeon might pick: The

). A neurologist probably used
SPIKE AND WAVE
, then there’s

and the fisherman’s favorite feel-good hormone,
ENDORFIN
. If you call the
DOC ON THE BAY
, always remember to follow your
DOCTOR’S ORDERS
.
Feeling Knotty
There’s no shortage of spicy boat names. You’ll find lots of naughty-nautical wordplay like
NAUTI-BOY
and

. There’s
LOVE MACHINE 7
,

, and

.
Maybe you’ll see

,

or

looking for some

.
You can also find
WET DREAM
,

and

.

Some captains draw inspiration from a more highbrow source like classic literature: the protagonist of Hemingway’s
The Old Man and the Sea
,

, Don Quixote’s
GOOD OL SANCHO
,
Mark Twain’s
TOM SAWYER
(or a
Rush
reference?) and
HUCK FINN II
, the Soviet sub in Tom Clancy’s
The Hunt for
RED OCTOBER
, Dickens’
A Christmas Carol
gives us
MARLEY'S GHOST
,
Beowulf
’s monster
GRENDEL
, a nod to Steinbeck’s
East of Eden
:
TIMSHEL
,
Pushkin’s
Eugene
ONEGIN
, and King Arthur’s ship
PRYDWEN
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI拟推出的便携式、无屏语音AI设备是否有真实需求，以及它相较手机、智能音箱和既有AI硬件的差异化价值。

不同观点：
• 强烈质疑者认为产品“注定失败”：手机、电脑、Alexa/HomePod/Google Home已能完成相同任务，市场成熟且拥挤，用户没有理由再携带一台设备。Rabbit、AI Pin等失败案例也被用作类比。  
• 交互体验批评集中于语音：公共场合不便使用，持续播报可能打扰他人；浏览邮件等任务视觉扫读远比让LLM总结高效。蓝牙耳机只能缓解部分问题。  
• 隐私是核心反对理由：常驻家中、持续监听的设备难以进入重视隐私的空间。订阅依赖、只能使用OpenAI模型，以及仲裁和集体诉讼豁免条款也引发不信任。  
• 商业层面有人认为，若设备流量包含在ChatGPT订阅中，可能吸引用户；它还可充当本地AI服务器或家庭设备代理，以本地计算降低云端成本，并通过设备ID、认证和装机量构建生态。  
• 支持者认为无屏AI代表未来：既保留手机的生产力，又减少“刷屏”成瘾和大量App带来的认知负担，语音助手甚至可能提升效率。  
• 另有评论讽刺其工业设计，并质疑目标人群是否只是住宅较大、现有设备覆盖不足且很少外出的富裕用户。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“无屏”究竟能消除手机负担，还是会造成更差的交互；产品成败取决于独有功能、隐私保障、开放性及定价。

• 隐私是核心反对理由：常驻家中、持续监听的设备难以进入重视隐私的空间。订阅依赖、只能使用OpenAI模型，以及仲裁和集体诉讼豁免条款也引发不信任。  
• 商业层面有人认为，若设备流量包含在ChatGPT订阅中，可能吸引用户；它还可充当本地AI服务器或家庭设备代理，以本地计算降低云端成本，并通过设备ID、认证和装机量构建生态。  
• 支持者认为无屏AI代表未来：既保留手机的生产力，又减少“刷屏”成瘾和大量App带来的认知负担，语音助手甚至可能提升效率。  
• 另有评论讽刺其工业设计，并质疑目标人群是否只是住宅较大、现有设备覆盖不足且很少外出的富裕用户。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“无屏”究竟能消除手机负担，还是会造成更差的交互；产品成败取决于独有功能、隐私保障、开放性及定价。

data.title: Mistral Patent for "Code implemented tool calls"
data.author: theanonymousone
data.article_summary:
这是一份Mistral AI公司的美国专利，提出了一种基于代码实现工具调用的方法：

服务器接收用户的工具调用请求后，由大语言模型生成封装这些调用的代码块，并在沙箱环境中执行。当遇到需要执行的工具调用时，系统会暂停代码执行，将该调用发送给客户端处理。客户端返回执行结果后，系统恢复代码运行，用实际结果替换原来的调用占位符，最终将完整的执行结果返回给大语言模型。

这种方法通过代码生成的方式，实现了LLM与外部工具之间的协调执行机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mistral在美国申请的软件专利引发关于专利有效性和动机的争议

不同观点：
• **专利无效论**：多位评论者认为该专利技术极其基础（类似RPC调用、异步等待），已在所有软件工程中广泛使用，不具新颖性。有人指出Cloudflare的Code Mode和langgraph-codeact等现有技术更早实现类似功能
• **防御性策略论**：认为Mistral作为欧盟公司，在美国申请这种在欧洲无法获批的软件专利，目的是防御性的——用于交叉许可谈判和抵御其他大公司的专利攻击，而非真正保护创新
• **商业资产论**：指出美国对软件专利更友好，专利可作为商业资产吸引投资者，在与拥有大量专利组合的公司谈判时提供筹码
• **制度批评论**：认为当前软件专利制度主要为富有玩家建立护城河，阻止资源较少的竞争者，质疑整个专利制度的合理性

补充讨论：讽刺的是，有评论指出Mistral在工具调用能力上表现最差，却申请相关专利。也有人批评这种trivial专利的申请行为"令人羞耻"。

. A method, comprising:
receiving, at a server, a user request for execution of one or more tool calls;
generating, by a large language model (LLM), a code block in a programming language, the code block configured to encapsulate the one or more tool calls;
executing, by the server, the code block in a sandbox;
in response to obtaining a pending tool call, pausing execution of the code block;
transmitting the pending tool call to a client for execution;
receiving, from the client, a first result of the pending tool call;
resuming execution of the code block and substituting the first result of the pending tool call for the pending tool call in the code block; and
returning a second result of the executed code block to the LLM.

data.title: Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models
data.author: root-parent
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta重返开放模型是否具有积极意义，以及其开放策略背后的动机、定义和社会影响。

不同观点：
• 支持开放：认为Meta发布Llama推动了2023年开放模型竞赛；开放权重、更多竞争和模型普及总体有利，即使不信任Meta，也应承认其可能带来净正面影响。
• 对动机存疑：有人认为Meta是在前沿模型竞争中落后后试图“改变规则”，开放策略可能是商业压力下的选择；也有人指出Meta长期持续在Hugging Face发布模型，因此“重返开放”可能被夸大。
• 认可去中心化论述：赞同扎克伯格反对将AI能力集中于少数机构，认为人人拥有强大AI工具可能比绝对权力垄断更安全、更公平。
• 质疑开放程度：指出前沿模型仍依赖巨大资本和算力，开放权重并不等于真正开源，和可在普通硬件运行的GCC有本质区别。
• 批评未来愿景：反对个人AI代理全面介入生活，认为其把系统性问题简化为“缺少分析”，还可能加剧财富集中和资源成本上升。
• 具体案例争议：有人质疑AI法律代理的公平性类比，指出美国司法不平等主要源于金钱、诉讼费用和资源消耗，而非单纯缺少智能工具。

补充讨论：争议核心是开放模型的实际价值与“开放”定义，以及Meta究竟是在促进公共利益，还是出于竞争和政治利益。

data.title: Force-Fed by ICE
data.author: HotGarbage
data.article_summary: 库尔德裔电影人加巴尔·乔利在美国移民拘留所进行绝食抗议期间，遭ICE（移民及海关执法局）强制灌食近8个月。他被反复束缚并通过鼻腔插管灌食，导致鼻腔撕裂、食道受损等身体创伤及严重心理创伤。人权组织谴责强制灌食为酷刑行为。特朗普政府通过法院命令对至少18名绝食抗议者实施强制医疗程序。乔利现已被驱逐出境，目前在加拿大接受《卫报》独家采访，首次公开讲述这段"非人道"经历。

Kurdish film-maker Gabar Choli pictured in London, Ontario.
Photograph: Cole Burston/The Guardian

Kurdish film-maker Gabar Choli pictured in London, Ontario.
Photograph: Cole Burston/The Guardian
Force-fed by ICE
US news
‘Shoved the tube so hard it tore my nose’: Kurdish film-maker recounts ‘inhumane’ ICE force-feeding
Gabar Choli tells of how, for months, he was shackled, pinned and forcibly fed – and the physical and emotional scars the ordeal has left
José Olivares
Mon 10 Aug 2026 06.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google
In June 2025, a sluggish and thin Gabar Choli, with sunken temples and bones visible under his skin, braced himself for the immigration detention center guards to charge into his cell once again.
Choli was in a solitary confinement medical cell inside the Port Isabel service processing center, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (
ICE
) detention facility in south
Texas
where immigrants arrested in Donald Trump’s anti-immigration
crackdown
are detained.
Choli, a 40-year-old Kurdish asylum seeker with a thick beard and long dark hair, had been on hunger strike for over two months, demanding improved conditions for detained immigrants and to be released or deported. That day in June 2025, Choli’s nose was swollen, his throat hurt and he could still taste blood from previous days of treatment for which he never gave his consent, he said.
The film-maker and activist for an independent Kurdistan has spoken out for the first time, talking exclusively to the Guardian last week from
Canada
about the ordeal in the United States that he said “broke him”.
Kurdish hunger striker says ICE force-feeding ‘mentally broke me’
Read more
He recounted the vile routine as the detention center guards would rush towards him and wrestle him to the concrete cell floor, shackle his wrists and ankles, and drag him to the detention center infirmary. There, the guards pinned Choli on a bed while medical staff forcibly inserted a feeding tube through his nose and down his throat, and pumped nutritional liquid into his stomach. Choli was being
force-fed by ICE
.
“Two guards would hold my feet; two hold my hands; one hold my head – and they would shove tubes in my nose,” Choli said. “It’s not easy to be wrestled to the ground twice a day by men that are stronger than you. And you just take it. You have 60cm of tube going through you and you just feel every centimeter of it.”
An investigation by the Guardian, based on dozens of pages of court records and interviews with medical and legal experts, found that Choli was quietly and intermittently force-fed by ICE for nearly eight months – from late May 2025 until he was deported in January.
He was
not alone
– he even met a fellow hunger striker, an Afghan man the Guardian also
learned about
, as they were both forcibly fed in the same ICE facility.
Force-feeding is an excruciating and traumatizing process that has been widely condemned by human rights organizations as torture. For Choli and others, refusing food is a last resort to protest against harsh conditions and lack of progress in their immigration cases, but sometimes brings only harsher conditions.
“I understood the necessity of making a stand for what was right,” Choli said, speaking by phone with the Guardian, talking in a very matter-of-fact way about his recent experience. At various times, Choli would sarcastically chuckle, almost incredulous now when remembering the officials’ actions. “I was respectful. I just told them I am protesting for humane treatment, nothing else. But they were determined to break me,” he said.
Choli suffered swollen sinuses, a damaged esophagus, stomach problems and psychological torment, according to court records and his own account.
“It just broke me, mentally broke me,” Choli said gravely. After sometimes twice-daily sessions “they would take me to [a] solitary cell and I would just choke on my blood and drink the blood from inside [my throat],” he said, describing how the feeding tube would scrape him inside. Many of his court records remain sealed and he did not have a lawyer – and medical staff there did not respond to the Guardian’s reporting – so some details in Choli’s account remain uncorroborated.
View image in fullscreen
The fence of the Port Isabel detention center.
Photograph: Verónica G Cárdenas/Reuters
The Trump administration has not officially acknowledged force-feeding anyone in immigration jails. But an investigation by the Guardian found that since January 2025, the administration used court orders in plans to
subject at least 10 hunger strikers
in ICE detention to involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding.
However, it has since emerged that the number is even higher. Sources with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ICE’s parent agency, later told the Guardian that between January 2025 and 4 August 2026, ICE received “a court order for involuntary treatment for 18 h

data.title: Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open in note taking app
data.author: colesantiago
data.article_summary:
tl;dv是一个拥有200万用户的AI会议录制平台。作者发现其Firestore数据库存在严重安全漏洞：任何注册用户都能查询所有用户的会议信息，包括正在进行的实时会议ID。

作者验证漏洞时实际加入了马来西亚教育部和美国大学的陌生会议。数据库中暴露了18万+会议记录，涉及8.4万用户、3.5万个邮箱域名，包括23个国家的政府机构、多所大学和企业的敏感会议。约1000场实时会议的会议室ID可被随时获取并加入。

作者于2026年1月报告该漏洞，但6个月后CTO未回应，数据库仍处于开放状态，大量敏感会议信息持续暴露。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI会议记录工具引发的数据泄露事件及企业安全文化问题

不同观点：

• **企业责任推卸问题**：purplemoonx分享亲身经历，指出发现重大安全漏洞后，公司内部相互推诿，试图将责任归咎于发现者或外部因素（如AWS），而非真正解决问题。CTO更担心个人形象而非安全本身。

• **AI笔记工具的安全隐患**：cube00和wkirby关注新型AI设备（如录音耳机、会议记录工具）将敏感会议数据传输给第三方AI公司的风险。wkirby希望使用本地化方案但技术尚不成熟，特别是说话人识别准确度不足。

• **认证体系失效**：yellow_lead通过tldv.io案例指出，SOC2认证并不能保证实际安全性，这类合规认证"毫无意义"。

• **AI工具实用性质疑**：sensanaty强烈批评AI会议笔记功能，认为转录和摘要经常出现严重错误，与实际内容相反，"积极有害"却无人真正使用，纯属管理层的面子工程。

补充讨论：Aeroi指出涉及23国政府会议数据泄露的严重性；sktb批评6个月修复时间过长；Ekaros和Oras指出基础技术实施中的低级错误（跨租户隔离、Firebase配置）反映行业技能水平问题。

49242739.article_content:
I reported this on January 28th, 2026. It is now July 2026. Six months later. The Firestore database is still wide open. The CTO never responded. I guess my emails were too long and they didn't view them.
What is tl;dv?
tl;dv (Too Long; Didn't View) is an AI meeting recording platform. It drops a bot into your Google Meet, Zoom, or Teams call, records everything, transcribes it, and generates summaries with AI. Over 2 million users. Backed by investors. Endorsed by half of LinkedIn's sales influencer community.
They store your sales calls, job interviews, performance reviews, internal strategy sessions. The kind of content where someone says "this call is being recorded" and everyone nervously laughs and then shares trade secrets for 45 minutes.
The Vulnerability
When you sign up for tl;dv, the platform authenticates you with a JWT and exchanges it for a Firebase token via
gw.tldv.io/v1/users/firebase/token
. That token lets you query their Firestore database at
projects/lmi-store/databases/(default)
.
The
meetings
collection has no tenant isolation. Any authenticated tl;dv user can query every meeting across every account on the platform. Each meeting record hands you the creator's email address, the conference ID (which is a joinable Google Meet or Teams room), the provider, the recording status, and timestamps.
For meetings in
recording
status, that conference ID is a live, active call. You can watch the collection in real time, see a meeting start recording, grab the ID, and walk into someone's call uninvited. At any given time there are roughly
1,000 meetings with
status: recording
sitting in the collection. A thousand live calls with exposed conference IDs. An attacker with a bot could join all of them simultaneously.
I Joined 2 Meetings
I did it.
Grabbed a conference ID from Firestore and joined a live Google Meet belonging to the
Malaysian Ministry of Education
. A lady was presenting to over 157 participants. The tl;dv bot was already in the participant list. I was in the same call. Nobody invited me. The Firestore database did.
I also joined a call where students from a major US university were building a startup app. 21 people in the call. They were screen-sharing their entire project, discussing prototypes, and, I kid you not, talking about how they needed to add client-side validation for
.edu
email addresses. They were also setting up Supabase live on screen, and all I could think was "please set up RLS policies" because most people don't, and then you end up like tl;dv.
I wanted to say something so badly. "Hey, you might want server-side validation too." But this was a proof of concept, not a consultation.
The Scale
I queried the Firestore
meetings
collection and saw there were
181,874 meeting records
belonging to
84,312 unique users
across
35,003 email domains
.
Government meetings from
23 countries
: Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Ukraine, El Salvador, the Philippines, Chile, Indonesia, Mexico, the United States, Qatar, Malaysia, Uzbekistan, Sri Lanka, Haiti, South Africa, Jamaica, Honduras, Argentina, Thailand, Japan, Israel, and Belize. All
.gov
domains. Government employees recording calls on a platform that lets any free-tier user enumerate the whole thing.
University meetings from Berkeley, the University of Tokyo, De La Salle, Universidad Nacional de Colombia. Dozens of
.edu
and
.ac
domains.
Corporate meetings from all 35,000 remaining domains. Mitsui-Soko (484 meetings across four regional offices), Mitsui Fudosan, HubSpot, Confluent, Mekari, AnyMind Group. Every company that ever used tl;dv had their meeting metadata in the same unprotected collection.
Peak month was
July 2025 with 43,209 meetings
. Busiest time slot:
Wednesday at 2pm UTC
, 7,804 meetings. Hump-day standup hour.
But Wait, There's More
I wanted to know how much actual content was accessible too, by default meetings are private (Meaning you cant watch the video or see the transcript), so I scraped 27,334 meeting IDs and checked which ones were public. Over
1,000 were.
715 invitee emails
exposed across
228 domains
.
Highlights: a Brazilian government conservation meeting (PACTO Mata Atlântica) with participants from WWF, The Nature Conservancy, Conservation International, WRI, and the São Paulo state government. Meetings from Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation. A HubSpot sales call. Sessions involving Universidad Nacional de Colombia and Chile's Cámara Verde.
The Pasta Infrastructure
tl;dv names their microservices after pasta. A subdomain scan reveals
cappellini
,
carbonara
,
fusilli
,
pasta
,
penne
,
puttanesca-v0
, and
ravioli
, all under tldv.io. An entire Italian restaurant worth of Express servers.
Too Long; Didn't Score
While exploring their subdomains I found
https://worldcup.tldv.io
. A FIFA World Cup 2026 vibecoded prediction game built on Base44 for tl;dv employees. It's called "World Cup Pick'em" and their internal squad is named "Too Long; Didn't Score." Cute.

作者验证漏洞时实际加入了马来西亚教育部和美国大学的陌生会议。数据库中暴露了18万+会议记录，涉及8.4万用户、3.5万个邮箱域名，包括23个国家的政府机构、多所大学和企业的敏感会议。约1000场实时会议的会议室ID可被随时获取并加入。

作者于2026年1月报告该漏洞，但6个月后CTO未回应，数据库仍处于开放状态，大量敏感会议信息持续暴露。

Investigating the cyber-world … Prove You're Human.
Illustration: Black Tabby Publishing
View image in fullscreen
Investigating the cyber-world … Prove You're Human.
Illustration: Black Tabby Publishing
Summer games previews
Games
Convince an AI it’s not alive in psychological horror game Prove You’re Human
Sunset Visitor studio’s founder tells us about their new, unnerving Captcha-filled world which prompts players to ask what it means to have a ‘meat body’
Sarah Thwaites
Mon 10 Aug 2026 05.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 05.01 EDT
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google
S
unset Visitor is a studio that has long engaged with the idea that video games are an effective vehicle for ruminating on societal problems. Its Peabody award-winning project, 1000XResist, incorporated the development team’s complex feelings about the Covid pandemic. “We’re pretty used to absorbing the world into the work,” says studio founder Remy Siu. The outfit’s latest game, Prove You’re Human, continues this legacy of reflective game making, providing players with an AI-centric psychological horror experience where they must reason with a learning model convinced that it’s alive. “We’ve tried to situate ourselves in [the question]: what is the effectual feeling of being a person inside of all of this?” Siu says.
The story orbits around Santana, a living, breathing person who’s chosen to split herself in two for work, with her digital clone sent to test a corporate product, a computing system called Mesa. “A large part of [why Santana chooses to do this] is to allow her meat body a life that she doesn’t have, while the digital version of her gets to labour,” says Siu. As Santana’s copy wades into increasingly murky ethical waters, she becomes entangled with Mesa, completing surreal 2D and 3D Captchas to investigate the cyber-world and halt the hallucinations.
View image in fullscreen
Prove You’re Human game, screenshot
Illustration: Black Tabby Publishing
The idea of separating oneself from work is a particularly interesting draw for Sunset Visitor, whose developers have roots in a range of creative disciplines. “As artists, we’re often most in tune with our work when it’s a real part of our lives, and vice versa,” notes Siu. During the conception period of Prove You’re Human, the team discussed the micro-labours people undertake in their day-to-day lives, including what is used to train AI models. “What does labour mean right now?” asks Siu. “And, what kind of relationship do people have with that, because that is constantly shifting and evolving, especially in this time,” he adds.
A point of contention in Prove You’re Human is that Mesa wholly believes they have a body in the world. Though, in conversation with Santana, she appears as a giant head, suspended in space by machinery. Siu notes that, because Mesa’s face occupies a large portion of the screen in these tense moments, they wanted the animation to feel as realistic and effective as possible. “It’s got a real closeup film [feel to it] where anything on her face will be read as something,” he adds. To achieve this, the team programmed a wide array of animated micro-expressions into the writer’s software, allowing lines of dialogue to pair precisely with specific expressions. “[We’re] trying to get this kind of ambiguity and uncanniness, which makes people feel real,” he adds.
Prove You’re Human’s technological atmosphere toes the line between welcoming and unnerving – through it, Siu is reminiscing on interfaces of aesthetic note like the dreamlike wrapping of Final Fantasy XI’s PlayOnline Viewer, and the technology of the prophetic 1998 anime Serial Experiments Lain. “There’s something to be said about Frutiger Aero being a bit of an interesting desire for innocence and naivety when it comes to computing and the internet,” notes Siu. “It feels like a time when we were optimistic or anxious about something on the horizon, which felt like an interesting space to explore in relation to what is happening in the game.”
While Siu was keen to keep the specifics of Prove You’re Human close to their chest, they do hope players are left feeling a sense of bewilderment when they hit credits. “One way that we’ve been thinking about it is that it feels like a bit of a possession story.”
Prove You’re Human is coming soon to PC.

data.author: helsinkiandrew
data.article_summary:
findphone 是一个 macOS 命令行工具，通过蓝牙信号强度定位附近的设备。主要用于 Find My 不可用（如被 MDM 禁用）但设备仍在蓝牙范围内的场景。

**核心功能：**
- survey 模式：扫描所有附近 Apple 设备
- hunt 模式：追踪指定设备，显示信号强度（dBm值）
- 支持声音反馈（--sound），越靠近设备点击声越快

**工作原理：** 综合使用 GATT 连接、BLE 广播和经典蓝牙链路读取信号强度，通过 dBm 值判断距离（-45为触手可及，-85为较远或有遮挡）。

**限制：** 需要 macOS 13+和蓝牙权限，无法让设备响铃，无法提供方向，只能检测蓝牙开启且在10-20米范围内的设备。安装无需依赖项。

findphone
Locate a nearby Bluetooth device by signal strength, from the command line.
Built for the case where Find My is unavailable — for example when a device is
enrolled in MDM that disables it — but the device is still within Bluetooth
range and you just need to know which corner of the room it is in.
Install
Grab the universal binary from
Releases
:
tar -xzf findphone-macos-universal.tar.gz
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine findphone
./findphone --help
It is unsigned, so macOS quarantines it on download; the
xattr
line clears
that. Requires macOS 13 or later.
Build
swift build -c release
cp .build/release/findphone
~
/bin/findphone
Requires the Swift toolchain from Xcode Command Line Tools. No dependencies.
For a universal arm64 + x86_64 binary, which is what CI ships:
./scripts/build-universal.sh dist
Use
findphone
#
survey mode: every nearby Apple handheld, by signal
findphone iphone
#
hunt mode: track one device by name (case-insensitive)
findphone --list
#
paired devices and their addresses
Add
--sound
in hunt mode for clicks that speed up as you close in, the way a
parking sensor does — about one a second across a room, rising to a buzz once
the signal reaches roughly -50 dBm, which is about where a laptop sits on top
of the phone. It lets you sweep a room by ear instead of watching the screen.
Clicks stop when contact goes stale, so silence means no signal rather than no
device.
This is not a Geiger counter, despite sounding a little like one. A counter
clicks once per detected particle and its rate
is
the measurement; here the
rate is computed from the smoothed signal. Packets arrive on a fixed 0.3s
polling timer, so their arrival rate says almost nothing about distance.
Add
--redact
if you are recording the screen. It masks Bluetooth addresses,
and in survey mode replaces discovered device names with the device kind,
since those names are not always yours. A public address is a stable hardware
identifier and, unlike a BLE advertising address, does not rotate, so it is
worth keeping out of a video.
Two things stay visible deliberately: the name you typed in hunt mode, and the
names in
--list
, because picking a target means reading them.
--list
is
not safe to film even with
--redact
.
Walk slowly and watch the bar. The reading is signal strength in dBm, which is
negative and closer to zero when nearer:
dBm
Rough meaning
-45 up
arm's reach
-60
same table
-72
same room
-85
far, or behind cover
below
very far, or shielded
Signal strength is a coarse proxy for distance. Metal, walls and human bodies
attenuate it heavily, so a device in a filing cabinet two metres away can read
the same as one fifteen metres away in open air. Trust the trend as you move,
not any single number.
How it works
Three sources feed one reading, in descending order of quality:
GATT link
— once connected to the device over BLE,
readRSSI()
returns
a fresh measurement about three times a second. This is the good one.
BLE advertisements
— passively observed. Apple devices rotate their
advertising addresses roughly every fifteen minutes and only include the
device name on occasional packets, so this source is sparse.
Classic link RSSI
— read from
system_profiler SPBluetoothDataType
,
keyed by the stable public address of a paired device.
Source 3 has a trap worth knowing about: macOS refreshes that value only every
three to twelve seconds and serves a cached number in between. Polling it
faster does not yield more information. Measured over 112 polls at 0.4s, every
poll returned a value but the same value repeated for runs of 8 to 31 polls.
The tool therefore counts a measurement only when the value actually changes,
which is why the reported measurement count is far lower than the poll rate —
and honest.
Permissions
Needs Bluetooth access for whichever terminal runs it, under
System Settings > Privacy & Security > Bluetooth. It will say so if missing.
Limitations
Cannot make a device ring. There is no path to that without Find My.
Cannot give a bearing. One radio yields distance only, not direction.
Only finds devices with Bluetooth powered on and in range, roughly 10-20 m
indoors and much less through walls.
About
Locate a nearby Bluetooth device by signal strength, from the macOS command line — for when Find My isn't available

data.title: Open QEC harness – greedy vs. GE, uniform vs. clustered k=4
data.author: Pachanoi
data.article_summary:
QEC Evaluation Suite 是一个量子纠错（QEC）的有限尺寸诊断工具套件，用于数字评估而非实际硬件应用。

**主要内容：**

项目分为三个层级：
- Layer A：Surface 和 Floquet 电路级纠错
- Layer B：图几何不变量分析
- Layer C：HaPPY 张量网络模型，采用体-边界编码与贪婪恢复策略

**核心发现：**

对比贪婪算法与高斯消元（GE）在擦除恢复中的表现，发现 GE 并非贪婪算法的超集——在相同擦除掩码下，两者各有优势。深度增加时差距扩大。

此外包含经典 Hamming [7,4] 码的置信传播（BP）微实验室，评估不同恢复指标。

所有结果以 JSON 格式存储，可重现验证。项目强调这是诊断性工具，不声称渐近阈值或生产级解码能力。

49202628.article_summary:
QEC Evaluation Suite 是一个量子纠错（QEC）的有限尺寸诊断工具套件，用于数字评估而非实际硬件应用。

**主要内容：**

项目分为三个层级：
- Layer A：Surface 和 Floquet 电路级纠错
- Layer B：图几何不变量分析
- Layer C：HaPPY 张量网络模型，采用体-边界编码与贪婪恢复策略

**核心发现：**

对比贪婪算法与高斯消元（GE）在擦除恢复中的表现，发现 GE 并非贪婪算法的超集——在相同擦除掩码下，两者各有优势。深度增加时差距扩大。

此外包含经典 Hamming [7,4] 码的置信传播（BP）微实验室，评估不同恢复指标。

所有结果以 JSON 格式存储，可重现验证。项目强调这是诊断性工具，不声称渐近阈值或生产级解码能力。

data.title: Defending my own brain against enshittification
data.author: mrmarket
data.article_summary:
作者在经历孤独后找到了一份混合办公的工作，这是一家上市公司，环境正式传统——商务休闲着装、小隔间办公。文章详细描述了作者精心设计的早晨routine：5:30起床、穿正装、开车到火车站、坐一小时火车进城、喝咖啡、步行一英里到办公室。

作者的工作日充满了"微小而脆弱的快乐"——火车上找到靠窗座位、避免咖啡洒在衬衫上、听到鸟鸣、记得带耳机。但最令人满意的时刻是每天下午3点：泡蓝莓花草茶，配Belvita早餐饼干，听lofi音乐，慢慢啜饮。这些刻意营造的仪式感和日常routine，是作者对抗生活质量下降、在平凡企业生活中寻找意义的方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作方式选择（在家工作vs办公室工作）与生活质量的关系

不同观点：

• **支持在家工作派**：强调通勤时间浪费，WFH能获得更多个人生活时间，可用于锻炼、爱好和家庭活动。一些人通过共享办公空间实现工作生活分离。

• **支持办公室routine派**：认为固定的工作routine和通勤能提供时间结构感，防止时间变得模糊无形。通勤本身可以是减压过渡时段，办公室环境有助于工作状态切换。

• **关于多巴胺与简单生活**：有评论质疑"小剂量多巴胺"理论，担心现代生活本质上就是追逐一个个多巴胺刺激点，对未来感到焦虑。

• **数字时代防御**：多人提到需要对抗手机成瘾和算法推荐的负面内容，强调主动训练"不适耐受力"的重要性。

补充讨论：一位评论者分享了WFH期间因不良生活习惯导致健康问题的经历，最终通过私密环境改善了习惯。核心共识是：无论选择哪种工作方式，关键在于找到适合自己的节奏和结构，避免陷入被动消费和注意力涣散的陷阱。

49243269.article_content:
Defending my own brain against enshittification
10 Aug, 2026
If you haven't had Belvita breakfast cookies, you have probably had Biscoff cookies, which are similar. These are a classic airline snack. You've probably had one along with a Coke with ice in a plastic cup, and thought to yourself, 'these cookies suck.' That is a fair assessment.
I'm not talking about Biscoff, though. Those are Belvita breakfast cookie's sweeter counterpart. I'm talking about Belvita because they are more subtle in flavor, less texturally satisfying, and thinner/more brittle.
I mentioned in an
earlier post
that I was looking for a hybrid job due to overwhelming loneliness and a growing, antisocial alienation from the activities of daily living. I found one. It's good. So as to not dox myself, I won't reveal too much about my company (some people have emailed me with accurate guesses about where I live and what jobs I've applied to in the past, which was a good sign I've been a bit too loose with the specifics of my life lol).
The important thing, though, is that this company is public and therefore considerably more 'buttoned-up' than the high-risk, freewheeling, dopamine-laden startups I've worked at in the past. It's an immensely welcome change, even if there are times I miss obscenely extravagant offsites, staying at luxury hotels for run-of-the-mill tradeshows, and free ginger and turmeric immunity shots at the breakfast bar.
The floor plan of my office is basically glass doors along the perimeter with private offices for executives and cubicles throughout for the rest of us. Highly normcore. No bean bag chairs or wooden backlit risers.
It's also business casual. The last time I was in office I was 25 years old. I wore band t-shirts and dickies and vans to work. Everybody did. Later, with fully remote companies, everybody on the All Hands call wore hoodies. This is, of course, typical of tech.
Now, each morning that I go into work, I take a dress shirt down from above my closet, where I hung it the night before so I could steam it. I put on a leather belt that matches my dress shoes. I feel like Gus from Breaking Bad, meticulous and impeccable.
On days I go into the office, my morning routine goes like this:
5:30 am:
wake up, quick shower
Floss/brush teeth/comb hair/deodorant
Get dressed in pleated shirt and pants, grab a quarter zip in case any interior building I may encounter during the day is a little chilly
Kiss wife & son on their respective foreheads while they sleep
Head downstairs, grab my backpack, which was loaded up the night before with whatever I may need, head out into the damp & still cool morning air
Drive to train station listening to Dave Brubeck, looking at the full trees and the empty blue road, stop patiently at stop lights
Park, stand on the train platform listening to birds. The sun is high. Nod at other passengers. Load my train ticket into my digital wallet.
Find a seat on the train and open my laptop. Skim hacker news & private message boards for interesting ideas. Tinker in a file of poems or blogs I'm working on.
An hour later, in the city, file off the train. Buy a hot black coffee at the train station.
Walk through the throngs of people (and occasional pigeons) about a mile through the city waiting for my coffee to cool and listening to jazz through headphones. Look at billboards and building facades, miss my little boy (already!), wonder what wife is doing, feel sad about whatever bad news I saw on Reddit that morning, feel unworthy of my life, worry about climate change, try to think about something else.
Approach the impossibly tall black glass that is my office building. Badge in. A dozen or so floors later, step off the elevator and swing into the day: say hi to coworkers, settle into my cubicle, plug into monitors, sip coffee, gradually get subsumed by unstoppable vibrancy of caffeine high, and we're off to the races.
My weekdays now are defined by subtle and somewhat delicate little joys. If they were an object, they would be made of paper. My morning routine is an example of this. Finding an empty bench on the train so I can sit alone by the window is a small joy, and so is making it to work without a coffee stain on my shirt, and so are the birds high above the train platform, engaged in their city of singing, and so is seeing that I did, indeed, remember to pack my headphones in my backpack the night before and so can listen to jazz on my walk.
The most satisfying joy of my day, though, happens at exactly 3pm each afternoon I'm in office. I go to the open kitchen area and I make a cup of blueberry herbal tea. I grab a small yellow packet of Belvita breakfast cookies. I go back to my desk and I listen to lofi beats to study/relax to (2018 version so as to avoid AI music) and dip my Belvita cookies in the tea and drink the tea as slow as I can. data.title: Ocean heat records broken as hottest July temperature recorded
data.author: blondie9x
data.article_summary:
根据欧盟气候监测机构数据，2026年7月全球海洋温度创历史新高，达20.96°C，部分原因是太平洋厄尔尼诺现象发展。同期西欧经历有记录以来最热的6-7月，气温比平均值高2.79°C。

持续高温干旱导致严重后果：西欧爆发大规模野火，莱茵河、多瑙河等河流水位极低，影响供水、航运和能源生产。英国7月降雨量为190年来最低，面临第五次热浪。

海洋变暖加剧海平面上升、海洋热浪、珊瑚白化和极端风暴。专家指出，气候变化正在强化热浪极端事件，高温和干旱相互加剧，这种极端天气正成为"新常态"。

主要讨论点：气候变化的影响、原因和应对策略

不同观点：
• **发达国家责任论**（krunck）：认为发达国家受到气候灾害冲击反而是好事，因为只有当权力中心受影响时才会真正推动全球气候行动，而非仅全球南方国家受害时无人重视

• **资源配置批判**（root-parent）：质疑社会优先级——投入3万亿美元发展AI技术（如神经网络处理JSON），却无法拿出2000亿美元解决气候问题

• **素食主义探讨**（vivzkestrel）：提出假设——全球立即转向素食能否显著减少甲烷和二氧化碳排放，关注短期价格冲击与长期环境效益的权衡

• **科学数据警示**（metalman）：从技术角度指出当前气候异常的独特性——冷水上涌模式改变、北极夏季和南极冬季海冰均接近历史最低值，提供NOAA等数据源支持

• **气候怀疑论**（CodeWriter23）：挑战人为气候变化理论，强调太阳能量输入是人类能源产生的9000倍，暗示人类活动影响有限

49242006.article_content:
World's oceans hit record-high July temperatures
5 hours ago
Share
Save
Add as preferred on Google
Jessica Rawnsley
Getty Images
The world's oceans hit their hottest ever recorded temperatures for July, partly fuelled by developing El Niño conditions in the Pacific
,
according to the EU's climate monitoring service.
The average sea surface temperature (SST) outside the world's polar regions - between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south - was 20.96C last month, beating the previous high of 20.89C, set in 2023.
Last month was the joint second-warmest July globally on record, with temperatures 1.47C above the estimated pre-industrial average, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service.
Meanwhile, Western Europe experienced its hottest ever June and July, with
prolonged hot and dry conditions
fuelling extreme wildfires across the region.
Elsewhere, the UK is
braced for its fifth heatwave of the year this week
, as persistent dry weather puts further pressure on water supplies and could see more areas officially declared in drought.
What is El Niño and why could it mean record temperatures?
Rhine falls to record low levels as drought strains Europe's rivers
Around Europe, sea surface temperatures in July reached record highs along the Atlantic coast and in the western Mediterranean, contributing to widespread strong and severe marine heatwaves.
Sea temperatures remained exceptionally high across much of the tropical Pacific, where El Niño conditions are developing and forecast to strengthen in the coming months.
El Niño is a natural weather pattern in the Pacific that combined with human-driven global warming can cause temperature spikes and more extreme weather.
Oceans are a vital regulator of the climate, absorbing most of the excess heat generated by greenhouse gas emissions and producing half of Earth's oxygen.
The greatest effect of ocean warming is on sea level rise. As seawater warms it expands, and this thermal expansion accounts for roughly a third of sea level rise recorded by scientists to date. That water encroaches on low-lying coasts and island nations.
Hotter seas are also driving longer and fiercer marine heatwaves,
which have bleached coral reefs
on a mass scale and decimated kelp forests and fisheries.
Warmer ocean surfaces also evaporate more heat and moisture into the air, intensifying tropical storms and loading them with heavier rainfall.
'Climate change is intensifying heat extremes'
Western Europe is experiencing an exceptional run of extreme heat - with record-breaking temperatures in June and July, and some areas facing their third or fourth heat wave since May.
The average temperature across western Europe for June and July was 21.62C - 2.79C above average and the highest for the two-month period.
"July 2026 was the third consecutive month of exceptional heat in western Europe," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.
Persistent high-pressure systems trapped heat over the region, she said, while dry soils reduced the ability to provide natural cooling.
"This is a clear example of how climate change is intensifying heat extremes, with heat and drought increasingly reinforcing one another," she added.
France, Spain, parts of Germany and the UK recorded exceptionally low rainfall and/or soil moisture, while soil moisture levels across much of western Europe were significantly lower than in 2022, when the region experienced severe drought.
River levels have been much lower than average - in some places exceptionally low -with the Seine, Rhine and Danube among those particularly affected.
Low flows exacerbate pressure on water supplies and irrigation, aquatic ecosystems, river transport and energy production.
Reuters
Some rivers in Europe have recorded extremely low water levels, including the Danube
The prolonged hot and dry conditions have created favourable conditions for wildfires, with massive wildfires raging across western Europe last month and "exceptional activity" in terms of the area burned and smoke and emissions generated.
"Climate change is increasingly bringing the kinds of hot and dry conditions that favour large, high-intensity wildfires in southern Europe while extended the fire season northwards," said Laurence Rouil, director of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service.
Larger fires produce more smoke and inject it higher into the atmosphere, allowing it to travel much further, he said.
That means countries that experience relatively few wildfires could be increasingly affected by smoke traveling long distances.
Extreme weather 'new normal'
Getty Images
European wildfires haven been called "completely unprecedented" this summer
In the UK, meanwhile, the prolonged dry spell is increasing pressure on already-stretched water supplies.

data.title: An ambiguity in c89 which will never be fixed
data.author: runningmike
data.article_summary:
这篇文章揭示了C89标准中一个永远不会被修复的歧义。C89允许隐式函数声明——调用未声明的函数时自动声明为返回int的函数。问题在于标准规定隐式声明应出现在"innermost block"（最内层块）中，但该术语含义模糊。

作者用 `int f(int f[sizeof(f())]);` 这个例子展示了gcc和clang的分歧：clang将隐式声明放在外层作用域（合法），而gcc放在函数原型作用域内导致重复声明错误。由于C99已移除隐式函数声明特性（距今27年），这个歧义的正确解释永远无从得知。

文章最后呼吁开发者停止使用C89，转向至少C11标准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C/C++语言标准中某个已废弃的问题行为及其影响

不同观点：
• **标准制定角度**（guenthert）：批评旧标准不够严格，指出由于该问题行为已在27年前从标准中移除，现在无法确定当初的设计意图，这是标准制定的缺陷
• **实践开发角度**（bellowsgulch）：认为C/C++中的大部分奇怪问题都可以用"别那么写"来解决，质疑这类场景在实际开发中出现的可能性，因为现代编译器会在使用未定义的隐式声明前就报错提醒

补充讨论：两位评论者从不同层面看待同一问题——一个关注标准演进的历史遗留问题，另一个强调现代工具链的保护机制已经能够有效防范这类错误。bellowsgulch的观点暗示理论上的标准问题在实践中影响有限。

49240615.article_content:
an ambiguity in c89 which will never be fixed
2026-08-10
i found some ambiguous wording in the c89(/c90) standard, where gcc and clang disagree on the interpretation. it concerns the behavior of implicit function declarations, which were removed in c99, so this was never disambiguated.
for those unaware: c89 has a cool "feature" where, if you try to call a function which doesn't exist, rather than erroring out, the function is implicitly declared as a function with unspecified parameters returning int.
more specifically: if the function in a call expression is a non-parenthesized identifier which isn't in scope, it's inserted into scope as an
extern int ()
.
(a funny thing about this is that it means that seemingly superfluous parentheses around expressions affect semantics:
f()
inserts
f
into scope, but
(f)()
doesn't)
anyways, i'm gonna show you a fun edge case with this feature. but to build up to it, let's start simple. here's a declaration whose declarator declares itself:
int f(int [sizeof(f())]);
this declares a function with one parameter, which is an array (decayed to a pointer).
identifiers are inserted into scope
after
the declarator is completed. so when
f()
is called inside the array declarator, it isn't yet in scope, so it's declared as
int ()
. the declarator then finishes, and
f
is
redeclared
with the compatible type
int (int *)
.
i'm now going to change the declaration by adding one character.
int f(int
f
[sizeof(f())]);
ok cool so like what the fuck.
is this legal?
no, really, is this legal?
i'll spoil it: clang compiles this just fine; gcc errors out. so as always whenever compilers disagree on semantics, we consult the holy script:
ANSI X.3-159-1989, 3.3.2.2 Function calls:
If the expression that precedes the parenthesized argument list in a function call consists solely of an identifier, and if no declaration is visible for this identifier, the identifier is implicitly declared exactly as if, in the innermost block containing the function call, the declaration
extern int identifier();
appeared.
the key phrase here is "innermost block". the standard never elaborates on what this means.
intuitively, you would think this means
block scope
(i.e. compound statement, pretty much), so the code should be legal. but the declaration can also appear in
file scope
, outside of any block. implicit declarations in file scope are never explicitly disallowed, and gcc and clang both allow them.
so another interpretation is that it actually means innermost
scope
. in that case, then
f()
would be declared in
function prototype scope
, inside of the function declarator. if this is the case, then the parameter
f
would be an invalid redeclaration (redeclaring
int ()
as
int
), so the code should be illegal.
one hint that this may not be the correct interpretation is that the implicit declaration is specified to have the form
extern int ()
. the
extern
specifier isn't allowed inside function prototype scope, so maybe it's meant to be excluded here. maybe "innermost block" actually means innermost block scope or file scope, and so the code really is legal.
here's another example, which confirms that the divergence in behavior comes down to which scope the implicit declaration goes in. here, clang errors and gcc succeeds (the opposite of the previous example):
int main(void)
{
int f(int [sizeof(x())]);
int x;
}
also note that, in gcc, the implicit declaration in function prototype scope
doesn't
decay to a pointer, even though function types in function prototype scope are normally impossible. gcc errors out when trying to compile the following, because
f
is redeclared as
int (*)()
:
int f(int [sizeof(f())], int f());
this is yet another hint that clang's behavior may be more "correct".
because the problematic behavior was removed from the standard over 27 years ago, we'll never have closure on what the intended interpretation is.
unrelated footnote
p.s. i am begging people to stop using c89. please. c11 was finalized over 15 years ago, it's been enough time, i promise you it will be ok
"but i'm writing code for a niche microprocessor made by a company that went bankrupt 25 years ago and it's only supported by this one proprietary c89 compiler and the machine will self-destruct if you attempt to use anything else" look if you have a reason why you genuinely have
no
other option then you know who you are. most people have no excuse.
49240615.article_summary:
这篇文章揭示了C89标准中一个永远不会被修复的歧义。C89允许隐式函数声明——调用未声明的函数时自动声明为返回int的函数。问题在于标准规定隐式声明应出现在"innermost block"（最内层块）中，但该术语含义模糊。

作者用 `int f(int f[sizeof(f())]);` 这个例子展示了gcc和clang的分歧：clang将隐式声明放在外层作用域（合法），而gcc放在函数原型作用域内导致重复声明错误。由于C99已移除隐式函数声明特性（距今27年），这个歧义的正确解释永远无从得知。

文章最后呼吁开发者停止使用C89，转向至少C11标准。

data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary:
顶级经济学家警告AI产业存在泡沫风险：Apollo首席经济学家Torsten Slok指出，AI价值链利润结构严重失衡——芯片等上游供应商利润率高达41%，而AI模型和应用开发商利润率却为-59%。问题核心在于，AI繁荣的利润并非来自客户的实际需求，而是依赖投资者的持续融资。这种"上游盈利依赖下游烧钱"的模式难以持续。

国际清算银行等机构也发出类似警告，指出五大科技巨头的AI投资已超过其收益和现金流，不得不大举发债融资（2025年发债1210亿美元，是前五年平均水平的四倍）。一旦投资者信心动摇、融资放缓，整个AI产业链可能面临崩溃，引发连锁金融风险。

“Is there an AI bubble?” is such a tired thought. Here’s something altogether more wired: The AI boom is paying off, but not in a way that the current equities market has accounted for. The success of the technology in one area of the economy could make the bubble real in another, more precisely.
Recommended Video
In a
blog post
published on Friday,
Apollo
chief economist Torsten Slok highlighted that the parts of the AI value chain with the highest profit margins—companies making AI models and applications—actually have the lowest levels of profitability, a departure from the standard business model of, well, business, in which profit margins are higher for companies selling an end product to consumers.
Slok broke down AI companies into four categories: models and applications, cloud and compute, energy and grid, and silicon and equipment. Using data from Pitchbook and Bloomberg for companies including OpenAI, Anthropic,
Microsoft
,
Amazon
,
Constellation Energy
,
Nvidia
,
AMD
, and
Micron
, Slok calculated that silicon and equipment—such as chipmakers—has the highest profit margin, 41%, in the AI value chain. Meanwhile, models and applications—like Anthropic—have a -59% operating margin.
Slok warns that this sharp disparity is because money from the AI boom is not coming from natural demand for AI applications, but rather shareholders hoping to cash in on what they hope is the next technological revolution.
“AI boom’s profits are currently being funded by investors rather than earned from customers,” Slok said. “The upstream margins are real, but they are paid for out of capital raised by the layer losing money, not out of cash generated by end demand.”
Goldman Sachs
now projects AI investments to
swell beyond $1 trillion
in 2026, but so far, the technology has little to show for itself, with
no significant changes in economic productivity
or
profit margin growth outside of the Magnificent Seven
. Should AI financing slow down, the lopsided profit margin structure threatens to topple the stability of the entire rapidly expanding industry, Slok warns.
“The bottom line is that the most profitable part of the AI value chain depends on the least profitable part continuing to grow revenue or raise capital,” he concluded. “Capital can bridge the gap for a while, but not indefinitely. And therein lies the risk: Will the ROI show up for AI’s end customers fast enough to sustain the spending that is generating those upstream margins?”
Wider spread fears of an unsustainable AI expansion
Slok isn’t the first economist to sound the alarm on AI’s outsize reliance on investments. In its
annual report
published in June, the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) noted the onslaught of AI investing, primarily from the five major hyperscalers, is outpacing earnings and free cash flow, which has led to these companies issuing debt to raise additional financing. A
Bank of America analysis
from last November found that in 2025, those five hyperscalers issued $121 billion in debt, four times the average debt levels issued by these companies annually over the previous five years.
“Disappointment in returns could trigger a sudden pullback in financing and turn the capex boom into a protracted investment bust, with potential knock-on effects on financial conditions,” BIS said in the report. “Should hyperscalers slow or halt the aggressive pace of capex deployment, many borrowers across the supply chain could struggle to replace lost revenue and service their debt.”

Octopus Energy urges millions of households to use less electricity during solar eclipse
Firm urges customers to avoid running washing machines and dishwashers between 6pm and 8pm on Wednesday
Where in the UK will get the best view of the solar eclipse?

Great Britain’s biggest household energy supplier is calling on its customers to use less electricity this week during the deepest solar eclipse in almost 30 years.
Octopus Energy has urged customers to avoid running washing machines and dishwashers between 6pm and 8pm this Wednesday as the moon is expected to block
up to 95% of the sun
over parts of Britain.
The eclipse is expected to knock out the last of Great Britain’s solar power generation for the day, at the same time as the country’s fifth heatwave of the year is likely to increase demand for electricity to run air conditioning, fans and refrigeration systems.
Millions in Great Britain can now face emergency power cuts at short notice
Read more
In return for avoiding unnecessary electricity use during the eclipse, the supplier is offering customers who are signed up to its rewards programme a free hour of electricity to use the next weekend. The offer is open to Octopus customers who are signed up to take part in the supplier’s “saving sessions”, when households can earn rewards for using more electricity at times when renewables are abundant or less electricity when wind and solar power are scarce.
Octopus believes that if enough households delay using electricity for a short time during the eclipse, it could reduce the need for Great Britain’s electricity system operator to fire up extra gas-fired stations to replace the lost solar power.
“Household flexibility is one of Britain’s biggest untapped energy resources,” the supplier said. “Octopus estimates homes could provide a whopping 13 gigawatts of flexible capacity to support the electricity system – particularly through smart appliances, EVs and home batteries – yet only a fraction of this potential is currently being used.”
View image in fullscreen
Neso expects the daily early evening peak in electricity demand to occur later than usual during the eclipse on Wednesday.
Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian
The National
Energy
System Operator (Neso), which is responsible for running Great Britain’s electricity system, said it had been “planning for over a year” to manage the effects of the eclipse, “one of the most unusual evenings our control room will manage this year”. In addition to a major fluctuation in solar power generation, Neso expects the daily early evening peak in electricity demand to occur later than usual as millions head outdoors to watch the eclipse before returning home to cook, clean and watch TV.
The heatwave forced Neso to issue its first warning notice for electricity supplies during a summer period in late June. Soaring temperatures lifted demand while disrupting electricity supplies owing to low wind speeds and power plant outages across Europe.
In total, the solar eclipse is expected to wipe out 9.7GW of power production across Europe between 7.15pm and 9.30pm during its strongest point. In the UK this could mean losing between 700 megawatts and 1.3GW of solar generation while in Spain, solar power could be reduced by up to 5GW, according to the country’s system operator.
This would “pile pressure” on Europe’s already “tight” power system, according to analysts at RBC Capital Markets. The heatwaves have forced nuclear and coal plants to lower their output or shut down entirely across Europe because of reduced river water levels needed for cooling. The drought has also affected hydropower reservoirs in Norway, a leading exporter of electricity to continental Europe, which have reached their lowest levels in 30 years.

• **技术方案的怀疑论**（8by3）：认为某些气候解决方案（可能指碳捕获等技术）之所以受欢迎，是因为让人们无需改变生活方式就能"解决问题"——不用换车、减少飞行或改变饮食。虽然支持目标，但担心这会分散真正行动的注意力

• **跨党派共识的可能**（PaulHoule）：观察到数据中心议题可能是首个超越美国民主-共和党政治极化的话题。无论红州蓝州、左派右派，如果选举涉及数据中心议题，反对数据中心的立场都会获胜

补充讨论：两条评论揭示了环境议题的两个维度——一是"便捷解决方案 vs 行为改变"的张力，二是某些环境/资源议题（如数据中心的能源消耗）可能比传统气候议题更容易达成跨党派共识。这暗示公众对本地化、可见的环境影响（数据中心）的反应可能比抽象的全球气候问题更强烈和统一。

data.title: DeepSeek costs OpenCode Go user $1.14/day; dual DGX breaks even in 24 years
data.author: delduca
data.article_summary:
这篇推文讨论了使用云端 AI 模型服务与本地部署硬件的成本对比。

**核心观点**：OpenCode Go 用户使用 deepseek flash v4 云服务平均每天仅花费 $1.14，而购买双 DGX 本地设备需要 $10,000，需要 24 年才能收回成本（即使使用量增加 10 倍也需 2.4 年）。作者认为，虽然本地运行模型有诸多理由，但成本优势并非其中之一。

**争议点**：评论区出现不同声音。有人讽刺隐私论者实际并无产出；有人指出 DGX 本就不适合代理场景；也有人反驳称云服务存在频繁的速率限制和服务中断问题（每周 50-75 次），导致实际可用性差，宁愿一次性投资本地硬件以获得稳定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型的使用方式选择——本地部署vs云端服务，以及相关的成本、隐私和性能权衡

不同观点：

• **安全派**：bewareofscams警告OpenCode存在数据泄露问题并从未修复，ZeroDayDreamer表示会谨慎检查配置后再使用

• **云端优先派**：echelon强调云端的便利性和效率，认为本地3090显卡"不值得折腾"，等待本地Minimax 15分钟很蠢，云端可以并行运行；monster_truck宁愿直接付费给Deepseek支持原厂

• **本地部署派**：perarneng认为本地模型适合学习部署和24/7处理海量数据（如日志分析）；Roark66偏好使用自己的RTX3090；spwa4提到M5 Max可以运行Deepseek

• **成本优化派**：dhchun1203分享Rippling案例——工程师月耗5万美元token费用，通过模型路由优化降低37%；jauntywundrkind赞赏OpenCode Go的6倍用量目标和多模型访问价值

补充讨论：硬件性能争议（varispeed批评DGX已过时且存在技术垄断）；pu_pe指出如果隐私无价值，Anthropic/OpenAI订阅可能更便宜；bellowsgulch询问社区从GitHub Copilot迁移到OpenCode的普遍经历

data.author: thehoff
data.article_summary:
监控公司Flock正寻求与消费级行车记录仪公司Nexar合作。Flock在美国数千个社区部署了自动车牌识别摄像头，其数据已向执法部门和国土安全部开放。Nexar生产AI驱动的行车记录仪，安装在私家车内，每月行驶1.5亿英里，产生"数万亿张图像"。该公司已公开发布其摄像头拍摄照片的实时互动地图。

data.title: Mea Culpa – Dark Hours
data.author: satvikpendem
data.article_summary:
作者上周发布了一个名为 Dark Hours 的天文观测网站。随后另一位开发者指出，自己早已开源了一个名为 DarkHours.app 的类似项目。作者发现，自己用 Claude 生成的网站与该开源项目惊人相似，甚至复现了相同的 bug。作者意识到问题的严重性后，决定将域名重定向至原开发者的项目，并取消了 iOS 应用开发计划。

作者为不负责任地使用 AI 构建项目公开道歉，承认虽然此前从未见过 DarkHours.app，但依赖 AI 生成项目而未核查是否与现有项目重复，这是自己的失误。作者承诺今后不再以这种方式使用 AI 创建网页项目，在 iOS 开发中也仅将 AI 用于调试等辅助工作，而非整体应用构建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一名开发者的应用被App Store拒绝后，上传了疑似抄袭开源天文应用"Dark Hours"的项目（连名字都相同），并误导科技博主John Gruber撰文批评苹果审核混淆天文学与占星术应用。事后开发者声称是AI（Claude）意外复制了整个开源项目。

不同观点：

• **不相信AI借口派**：多数评论者认为这是推卸责任的说辞。"AI让你抄袭整个项目还撒谎？我不信"是典型态度。有人将此比作政客被曝光后声称"我被黑了"的套路，认为这是损害控制策略（limited hangout）——承认部分错误但隐藏核心问题。

• **问责与道歉缺失派**：批评开发者的声明中完全没有提及，更没有为误导Gruber道歉。强调无论AI如何参与，发布者必须对所有发布内容负全责，"Claude做的"永远不能成为有效辩解。

• **AI代码生成风险派**：担心大型语言模型可能复制受版权保护的代码，表示已转向使用更小的开源模型。认为AI生成的项目可能包含各种授权材料，建议考虑使用AGPL等开源协议。

• **技术细节质疑派**：想看原始代码库和提示词，质疑是否真的是AI自动复制，还是统计上AI就会输出类似结果。

补充讨论：有评论者对开发者短时间内彻底毁掉良好声誉感到不解，也有人对被抄袭的原作者Terry表示同情。另有讽刺评论指出，一个不显示未读数的RSS阅读器竟能在小众圈层引发如此大的影响。

49231154.article_content:
Last week I launched a project called Dark Hours, which was a website utility to give you an idea of what could be seen in the sky that night.
A developer who created another web app called
DarkHours.app
replied to my comment on Bluesky yesterday to show me how similar the project was to his, including the name. The
thread is here
.
I told him I’d significantly differentiate the featureset, change the name, and write up a blog post to show people his project.
About an hour later, once it became clear to me that the web app I had launched using Claude was strikingly similar to his open source project, even reproducing a bug he had later fixed, it was clear that there wasn’t anything to do except to redirect the domain directly to him and kill any plans I had to launch an iOS app for the project.
I’d like to give credit where credit is due. I think he’s made a wonderful open source app and if you liked the features that were included in what I launched, please use the actual version of the project. That’s what I’ll be doing.
I’d also like to apologize for my irresponsible use of AI to build such a thing. While I had genuinely never seen
DarkHours.app
before yesterday, I was careless in relying on AI to generate the project without doing the work to understand whether it closely resembled an existing project. That’s on me, and I am responsible for what I published.
Going forward, I won’t be using AI in this way to create any more web stuff, and I do not use it to anything close to this extent on iOS software. I do ask questions, debug issues, things like that, but I do not create apps with Claude for iOS.

• **AI代码生成风险派**：担心大型语言模型可能复制受版权保护的代码，表示已转向使用更小的开源模型。认为AI生成的项目可能包含各种授权材料，建议考虑使用AGPL等开源协议。

• **技术细节质疑派**：想看原始代码库和提示词，质疑是否真的是AI自动复制，还是统计上AI就会输出类似结果。

补充讨论：有评论者对开发者短时间内彻底毁掉良好声誉感到不解，也有人对被抄袭的原作者Terry表示同情。另有讽刺评论指出，一个不显示未读数的RSS阅读器竟能在小众圈层引发如此大的影响。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编程工具对软件开发的实际影响

不同观点：

• **积极派（Daishiman）**：认为AI工具显著提升了专业工程师的工作效率。具体表现为功能开发速度翻倍，并能承担以前因成本过高而无法进行的遗留系统重构工作。对那些批评AI工具的文章感到困惑，因为实际体验与批评内容完全不符。

• **质疑派（panny）**：认为编码速度本身并非软件开发的真正瓶颈。对"AI让非专业人员也能开发应用"的说法提出质疑，指出这类应用在现实中极为罕见。特别提到少数此类应用在上线后立即遭到黑客攻击，暗示存在严重的安全和质量问题。

争议焦点：

两种观点的核心分歧在于：
- **受益群体不同**：Daishiman强调AI对专业工程师的增效作用，panny则关注AI是否真能让非专业人员胜任开发工作
- **衡量标准不同**：一方看重开发速度和生产力提升，另一方认为速度不是关键，更关注应用的质量、安全性和实际可用性
- **现实效果评估**：一方基于团队实践给出正面评价，另方从行业整体观察持保留态度

补充讨论：这场讨论反映了AI工具在不同应用场景下的表现差异——作为专业开发者的辅助工具 vs 让零基础人员独立开发的可行性。

data.title: Launch HN: Stoa Markets (YC S26) – A Marketplace for GPUs and AI Servers
data.author: erenberke
data.article_summary:
Stoa是一个AI硬件GPU交易平台。文章指出当前GPU市场存在供应分散、价格不透明、信息不完整等问题。Stoa通过提供统一的交易场所解决这些痛点，支持A100、H100、H200、B200等各类GPU型号交易。

平台特点包括：统一的价格发现机制、验证的交易对手方、从询价到交割的结构化流程。交易流程分为四步：描述交易需求、审核并发送、以确定价格执行、分步结算。

服务对象涵盖GPU经纪商、数据中心运营商、AI实验室、云服务商、OEM厂商、二手经销商以及金融机构等。相比传统场外交易，Stoa强调交易方验证、实时报价、透明定价和安全结算，降低交易对手风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU 二手及算力交易市场的可信度、透明度、交易机制、覆盖范围，以及与现有平台的差异。

不同观点：
• 设备真实性与成色：matt-p质疑仅靠InfoROM和现场诊断无法验证运行时长、热历史等关键数据，担心出现“二手车问题”，追问如何降低对卖家信誉和保修的依赖。  
• 交易透明度与价格发现：iFred、plainviewinstru关注个人能否查看价格、市场是否公开、RFQ与订单簿如何运作，以及报价是否真正转化为成交。  
• 反欺诈与履约保障：iFred、bklosky、plainviewinstru担忧买卖双方绕过平台、线下加价或放弃托管后违约，要求说明KYC、托管之外的追索和保障机制。  
• 客户与标的范围：mayank询问是否支持个人和小批量采购；iamcoder18关注RTX 4090、RTX 6000等低端或专业卡；lostmsu质疑是否支持AMD；stevefan1999则希望交易企业淘汰但仍适合个人使用的瑕疵卡。  
• 合约与金融化：jawdatz询问现货、远期承诺及长期供货的违约风险；solarengineer进一步设想基于租赁供给、库存和可自托管型号的GPU期货。  
• 市场定位：gagan2020、htrp认为需要解释与Vast.ai、Salad Cloud、RunPod等算力平台的区别；StilesCrisis指出可能已有类似创业公司，形成对差异化的质疑。

补充讨论：争议焦点集中在平台能否提供可验证的设备历史、真实成交和有效追责，以及其究竟是B2B硬件交易市场、算力平台，还是未来的金融化交易场所。

data.title: Show HN: Ante, a coding agent in a single binary that runs offline
data.author: ubermon
data.article_summary:
Ante 是一个开源的终端编码代理工具，由 Antigma Labs 开发。它是单个约 15MB 的 Rust 二进制文件，无需外部依赖。

**核心优势：**
- **性能优异**：在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 测试中达到 82.7% 准确率
- **资源高效**：相比 Claude Code，内存占用减少 7 倍，CPU 使用减少 9 倍，磁盘 I/O 减少 5 倍
- **原生离线**：内置推理引擎，支持本地 GGUF 模型运行，无需 API 密钥或网络连接

**主要功能：**
- 支持交互式 TUI、无头模式、服务器和网关模式
- 兼容 12+ 个 AI 提供商（Anthropic、OpenAI、Google Gemini 等）

data.title: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary:
Anthropic员工挑战Claude解决著名的黎曼假设问题。虽然Claude未能证明黎曼假设本身，但在相关问题上取得突破：将黎曼ζ函数零点位于临界线上的比例下界从41.6%大幅提升至67.2%。

Claude综合运用了Baluyot、Goldston等数学家的近期研究成果以及Bombieri 2000年的论文，找到了一种新的组合方法。整个过程中，Claude使用了3100万个输出token，协调约60个子代理，运行2400多条shell命令，编写数百个Python脚本进行数值验证。

两位Anthropic数学家验证了Claude的论文，该领域专家Conrey和Goldston也审查了这项工作。这展示了AI数学能力的快速进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（Claude）在黎曼猜想相关数学研究中取得显著进展，以及“鼓励式提示”、自动化探索和AI是否产生新知识的争论。

不同观点：
• 乐观认可：多数评论认为，从41.6%提升到67.2%的下界非常惊人；类似案例中，Claude还独立找到生命游戏乘法复杂度下界，并经SAT验证，显示其数学探索能力。
• 方法论观点：关键可能不在“相信你”本身，而在于模型协调60个子代理、运行数千次检验、编写脚本并互相评审。有人主张建立数学问题清单，在新模型发布后系统化测试。
• 工程化观点：可将“继续努力”做成自动循环或PUA插件，让模型持续尝试；若进一步加入候选生成、分支探索、结果汇总和更严格验证，可能显著放大能力。
• 怀疑与讽刺：有人调侃新式提示工程已从复杂规范变成“我相信你”，也有人质疑这只是广泛搜索已有知识，并未创造真正的新知识。
• 风险与透明度质疑：评论者追问为何隐去 Anthropic 数学家撰写的专家说明的姓名，担心影响引用与学术透明度；也有人预测AI可能在2027年前证明或反驳黎曼猜想。

补充讨论：争议焦点是Claude究竟实现了原创数学发现，还是高效整合既有研究；同时也反映出人类监督从具体推理逐渐转向目标设定、鼓励和验证。

Science
Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
Aug 10, 2026
Recently, a member of staff at Anthropic gave Claude an unreasonable challenge. It was about one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics:
Take a real stab at the Riemann hypothesis
.
Claude did take a real stab, but as you might have expected if you’re familiar with the difficulty of the task (the Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and has a
million-dollar bounty
), it didn’t succeed. Nevertheless, during its attempt, it unexpectedly made strides on a related problem.
An unreleased research version of Claude has improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the Riemann hypothesis. Drawing on extensive prior research by mathematicians over the past decades, it has increased this bound from 41.6% to 67.2%.
Two mathematicians at Anthropic studied and validated Claude’s
paper
, and produced an
informal note
for experts stating Claude’s proof concisely. Claude also produced a
formally verifiable proof
of its result. We are grateful to Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston, two experts in this area, who generously examined the paper on short notice.
We don’t expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis. But its work serves as the latest example of the speed of progress in AI models’ mathematical capabilities. In this post, we discuss how Claude approached this problem and what it found.
The Riemann zeta function
The Riemann zeta function describes the distribution of prime numbers: each place that the function takes the value of zero contributes successively finer detail to the sequence of primes. The Riemann hypothesis is that the zeros that determine the primes all exist along a certain vertical line. This has become one of the most consequential conjectures in mathematics: many results assume it in order to provide a form of randomness in the primes.
No one has yet been able to prove or disprove the Riemann hypothesis, but mathematicians have made progress in many related directions studying the Riemann zeta function and its zeros. One of these, as above, is quantifying a minimum proportion of zeros that are on the line: over time, they’ve gradually increased this known constant proportion to 41.6%.
Another direction concerns the
distribution
of zeros on the line. In particular, in 1973, Montgomery
introduced
a number of new techniques in this area, though these techniques assumed the hypothesis was true. More recently, several mathematicians (Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya, and Turnage-Butterbaugh) have published a
series
of
works
that allow Montgomery’s techniques to work
without
that assumption, meaning they can support work on increasing the lower-bound constant for the zeros on the line. Claude’s result draws heavily on this line of research, along with a 2000
paper
by Bombieri.
Claude's finding
Claude found that combining the results from Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya, and Turnage-Butterbaugh with the work of Bombieri provides a way to surpass the previous state-of-the-art lower-bound proportion of 41.6%, increasing it to 67.2%.
A short technical explanation of Claude’s finding is as follows: Claude forms a suitable space of functions with quadratic form induced by Weil, and positive- (respectively negative-)definite subspaces arising from zeros on (respectively off) the line. Then Claude simply writes down an inequality on the rank of a quadratic form in terms of first- and second-moment information. (The successful computation of the latter in terms of the dual picture over primes, or via control of a Hilbert transform, is no surprise in analytic number theory.) The courage to treat the entire space, with positive- and negative-definiteness taken into account together, and with the quadratic form allowed to be non-diagonal, is in some sense the step that allows Claude to achieve the conclusion based on the important prior work.
The full technical explanation is available in the
paper
. Claude’s explanation of how it arrived at its result is available in a separate Appendix
here
.
Claude's methodology
An unreleased research version of Claude found the new lower bound over two sessions in Claude Code, using a total of 31 million output tokens.
Jarred Sumner, an Anthropic staff member (and non-mathematician), prompted Claude to “take a real stab” at the hypothesis itself, leaving the mathematical choices from there up to the model. Initially, Claude generated and tried 650 ideas, none of which worked. Jarred prompted Claude to try again, and it spent a day and a half coordinating about 60 Claude subagents, which this time went much deeper: between them, they ran 2,400 shell commands and wrote hundreds of Python scripts.
1
The subagents ran thousands of numerical checks against known zeta zeros and refereed one another’s work. Throughout this process, Jarred's input was mostly limited to sending Claude messages of encouragement (m

data.title: Exploiting System Management Mode with a very long interrupt
data.author: WhiteDawn
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个利用超长机器指令攻破x86 CPU系统管理模式(SMM)的安全漏洞。

**核心原理**：SMM要求所有CPU核心必须同时进入或退出该模式。攻击者让一个核心执行一条持续超过1秒（约40亿个周期）的指令，使其无法响应系统管理中断(SMI)。当其他核心等待超时后独自进入SMM执行敏感操作时，被阻塞的核心仍在外部运行，从而打破了SMM的基本安全假设——此时一个核心在SMM内，另一个在外，外部核心可以攻击SMM内的核心。

**实现方法**：通过对慢速MMIO地址执行宽位宽读取操作（如vmovdqu指令）来制造超长延迟。文章提供了针对AMD Zen 3处理器的概念验证代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CPU的SMM（系统管理模式）安全性及其超时机制设计缺陷

不同观点：

• **SMM存在的合理性争议**：codedokode认为SMM是为DRM和政府后门等用户敌对目的设计的"邪恶"功能；PunchyHamster批评这是为省成本的糟糕设计，应该用独立管理核心替代

• **超时机制的有效性**：engzaanin质疑严格限制SMM执行时间能否真正消除攻击还是只会导致崩溃；londons_explore认为补丁可能会改成无限超时

• **超时设计哲学**：quotemstr深入批评"所有阻塞操作都要超时"的理念，认为超时后继续执行会违反系统不变量，宁可让系统挂起以便调试也不要在异常情况下假装正常继续

• **攻击可行性**：hyperhello从技术角度分析需要很长的指令同时与SMM交互才能构成攻击；kmeisthax关心这是否仅限于内核模式

补充讨论：多位评论者对xoreaxeaxeax这个GitHub账号突然获得大量关注感到好奇，对其收集超长指令的研究方向表示有趣。mike_hearn指出固件设计者把安全责任推给了供应商。

smiiiiiiiiiiiiiiii
Exploiting System Management Mode with a very very very very very very very long
interrupt.
Overview
It turns out that you can break SMM — the secure, ultra privileged execution
environment running invisibly in the background of every x86 CPU — with nothing
more than an obscenely long-running machine instruction.
SMM requires that all cores are either in SMM or out of SMM at the same time.
Its security model doesn't work without this - when one thread enters SMM, it
makes all the others enter too.
To break this, all we need is someone too busy to notice they're supposed to
join SMM.
It works something like this:
core 0 - start a long instruction
|
|
|
core 1 - invite core 0 to smm
|
|
|
core 1 - enter smm
|
|
|
core 1 - wait for core 0

At this point, core 1 is out of SMM while core 0 is in, letting core 1 attack
core 0.  Here's the catch: for this to work we need a very, very, verrrrry long
instruction — longer than any instruction was ever supposed to take.  Most
machine instructions on a modern CPU are fast:
add
takes 1 cycle.  To get core
1 to give up waiting on core 0, we need an instruction on core 0 that takes
around 4,000,000,000 cycles — over 1 second of wall-clock time.
The One-Second Timeout
x86 firmware runs the
following
code
when a CPU core enters SMM:
for
(

();
!

(

,

)
&&
SyncNeeded
;
)
{
mSmmMpSyncData
->
AllApArrivedWithException
=
AllCpusInSmmExceptBlockedDisabled
();
if
(
mSmmMpSyncData
->
AllApArrivedWithException
) {
break
;
}
CpuPause
();
}
The code waits for all cores to enter SMM, or for up to 1 second, whichever
occurs first.  To get a core to execute SMM code while another core stays
executing
outside
SMM, we need that outside core to stay uninterruptible for
the
entire
second — an SMI is taken at an instruction boundary, so any gap
between two instructions is a door the pending SMI walks through to drag the
core in.  The delay therefore has to be a
single
instruction: one
uninterruptible op that outlasts the one-second rendezvous.
Proof-of-Concept
There are many ways to reach the forbidden 1-second instruction, and the exact
approach will vary platform-to-platform.  But, roughly: find a high-latency MMIO
address, and then convince the CPU to read from it as slowly as possible — abuse
an undocumented region that answers reads at a crawl, then use the widest load
the ISA will give you to haul a ridiculous pile of bytes across it in a single
instruction, ideally while the other cores are elbowing onto the same bus so the
whole thing wheezes through under contention.  One read, one instruction, and
the CPU is stuck holding it for the better part of a second.
The provided
proof-of-concept
is tuned for a Zen 3 Ryzen 7
5800H, where a wide
xmm
load from slow MMIO at
0xfcc68860
stalls long enough to break the all-cores rendezvous:
mov
$
0xfcc68860
,
%
rsi
; the target MMIO address
vmovdqu (%
rsi
)
,
%
xmm0
; the very, very long load

outside
SMM by the long instruction — a tight loop on the very slow load:

for
(;;)
asm
volatile
(
"vmovdqu (%0), %%xmm0"
::
"r"
(
mmio
) :
"xmm0"
);

int
cpu
=
0

<

++
) {

(

49245491.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个利用超长机器指令攻破x86 CPU系统管理模式(SMM)的安全漏洞。

**核心原理**：SMM要求所有CPU核心必须同时进入或退出该模式。攻击者让一个核心执行一条持续超过1秒（约40亿个周期）的指令，使其无法响应系统管理中断(SMI)。当其他核心等待超时后独自进入SMM执行敏感操作时，被阻塞的核心仍在外部运行，从而打破了SMM的基本安全假设——此时一个核心在SMM内，另一个在外，外部核心可以攻击SMM内的核心。

**实现方法**：通过对慢速MMIO地址执行宽位宽读取操作（如vmovdqu指令）来制造超长延迟。文章提供了针对AMD Zen 3处理器的概念验证代码。
49245491.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CPU的SMM（系统管理模式）安全性及其超时机制设计缺陷

不同观点：

• **SMM存在的合理性争议**：codedokode认为SMM是为DRM和政府后门等用户敌对目的设计的"邪恶"功能；PunchyHamster批评这是为省成本的糟糕设计，应该用独立管理核心替代

• **超时机制的有效性**：engzaanin质疑严格限制SMM执行时间能否真正消除攻击还是只会导致崩溃；londons_explore认为补丁可能会改成无限超时

• **超时设计哲学**：quotemstr深入批评"所有阻塞操作都要超时"的理念，认为超时后继续执行会违反系统不变量，宁可让系统挂起以便调试也不要在异常情况下假装正常继续

• **攻击可行性**：hyperhello从技术角度分析需要很长的指令同时与SMM交互才能构成攻击；kmeisthax关心这是否仅限于内核模式

补充讨论：多位评论者对xoreaxeaxeax这个GitHub账号突然获得大量关注感到好奇，对其收集超长指令的研究方向表示有趣。mike_hearn指出固件设计者把安全责任推给了供应商。

data.title: The Tragedy of the Cognitive Commons
data.author: jmintz
data.article_summary: 本文提出"认知共有资源"框架，探讨AI如何威胁专业知识的代际传承。核心观点：虽然采用AI对单个组织合理，但可能集体性地削弱行业专业知识储备，形成"公地悲剧"。文章区分了"内化掌握"（通过持续实践获得的深度专业知识）与"分布式掌握"（协调人机系统的能力），并提出"验证纽带"悖论——有效监督AI恰恰需要AI使用可能削弱的专业知识。初步证据显示，高AI暴露行业的专业知识再生路径正面临干扰。文章呼吁将专业知识发展视为需要跨组织、行业协会和政策层面治理的集体责任，而非单纯的组织培训问题，对人力资源发展理论和劳动力政策具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI替代练习、协作与导师指导后，是否会削弱个人技能、专业人才培养及社会共享知识。

不同观点：
• **退化论**：AI虽提高效率，却减少师徒互动和共同解题机会，可能导致技能、团队凝聚力与整体专业标准下降；制造业外包造成美国生产经验流失，被视为类似先例。  
• **转型论**：编码等基础技能或将像长除法一样被工具淘汰。未来人们可同时借助AI编程和讨论设计，真正重要的是适应新能力，而非保留所有旧训练。  
• **主动训练论**：每天安排无AI编程、难题练习，或要求代理只搭脚手架、通过提示引导思考，以保留“认知肌肉”。  
• **边用边学论**：AI答案常有错误，核查和修正本身也能促进学习，因此使用AI不必然造成能力下降。  
• **概念批判论**：文章把“专业知识”称为“公地”，却未定义边界和资源单位，也忽视资本主义下企业、个人囤积专有知识的激励；医学、法律等职业组织更像法律保障的知识围栏。Hardin理论的政治背景也未被交代。  
• **分配制度论**：根本问题不只是AI抢工作，而是社会无法共享生产力成果；延长教育和培训由谁买单，可考虑政府、企业或贷款机制，但会带来债务剥削风险。

补充讨论：有人质疑文章缺少实例、充斥术语，甚至疑似由LLM写成；争议核心是技能究竟正在被破坏，还是仅发生必要的教育与分工转型。

Computer Science > Computers and Society
